q: What type of chair is ideal for the waiting area in the lobby?
n: Since there is a releasing office, there would likely be a queuing system. Therefore, a gang chair is the most ideal for this scenario. Gang (beam) seating joins several seats on a common beam. It is durable, easy to clean around and space-efficient, so it is the standard for public waiting areas such as government lobbies. Source: Time-Saver Standards for Interior Design (Public Seating); Neufert, Architects' Data.

q: The number of zones of a walk-through metal detector refers to its
o: Number of people it can handle
n: A multi-zone walk-through metal detector divides the archway into detection zones. The zone count describes how precisely it pinpoints where on the body an object is. Source: NIJ Standard-0601.02 (Walk-Through Metal Detectors); manufacturers' specifications.

q: What type of ceiling is ideal for a conference room?
n: A convex ceiling diffuses sound evenly across a conference room. A concave ceiling focuses reflections into hot spots and echoes. Source: Egan, Architectural Acoustics (Room Shape and Reflections); Long, Architectural Acoustics.

q: Which type of door shall be avoided as an exit door?
n: Revolving, sliding and overhead doors shall not be used as exit doors. Revolving, sliding and overhead doors are not accepted as required exit doors. Exits must be side-hinged swinging doors that open in the direction of egress. Source: RA 9514 (Fire Code) 2019 RIRR, Div. 10.2.5 (Doors); NFPA 101, Sec. 7.2.1.

q: To instill order and integrity, what color should be incorporated in the lobby's interior color scheme?
n: Blue is associated with order, trust, stability and integrity. That suits the lobby of a public office. Source: Mahnke, Color, Environment and Human Response; Ching, Interior Design Illustrated (Color Psychology).

q: What comes after the notice to proceed?
n: Once the Notice to Proceed is issued, the contractor mobilizes: people, equipment and temporary facilities are brought to the site. Source: RA 9184 Revised IRR (Notice to Proceed and contract implementation); UAP SPP Doc. 301.

q: Which of the following is placed outside the building?
n: The ACCU (air-cooled condensing unit) rejects heat outdoors, so it sits outside the building. FCUs, AHUs and evaporators are indoor components. Source: ASHRAE Handbook – HVAC Systems and Equipment (Split Systems).

q: What is the ideal configuration of pathwalks considering accessibility of blind people?
n: Pathways for blind users should be simple and predictable, with right-angle turns and corners, guiding edges and warning blocks. Winding routes and breaks disorient them. Source: BP 344 2024 Revised IRR (Walkways and Tactile Guidance); ISO 21542.

q: In subdivision development, where should the Certificate of No Objection be acquired?
n: Subdivision applications need a certificate of no objection or barangay clearance from the barangay where the project is located. Source: Local Government Code (RA 7160), Sec. 152(c) (barangay clearance); DHSUD/HLURB permit requirements.

q: What is the maximum number of units per cluster of row houses?
n: BP 220 allows up to 20 row-house units per block or cluster, and no cluster may be over 100 m long. Source: BP 220 Revised IRR, Design Standards – Row Houses.

q: There are only two seismic zones in the Philippines. Which province is largely in Seismic Zone 2?
n: NSCP places the whole country in Seismic Zone 4 except Palawan (with the Sulu archipelago area), which is Zone 2. Source: NSCP 2015, Sec. 208.4.4 (Seismic Zone, Figure 208-1).

q: What type of foundation is ideal for a loam soil?
n: Loamy soil is ideal for construction of isolated pad footing. Loam with fair bearing capacity carries light to moderate loads on shallow isolated pad (spread) footings. Piles and piers are for weak or deep soils. Source: Das, Principles of Foundation Engineering (Shallow Foundations); Ching, Building Construction Illustrated, Ch. 3.

q: What type of mortar is considered high-strength?
n: Type M mortar has the highest compressive strength (about 17 MPa) of the ASTM C270 types M, S, N, O and K. Source: ASTM C270 (Mortar for Unit Masonry).

q: What should be the thickness of concrete cover for beams and columns?
n: Cast-in-place beams and columns not exposed to weather or earth need 40 mm of clear cover. Source: NSCP 2015, Table 420.6.1.3.1 (Specified Concrete Cover); ACI 318.

q: What is the usual ratio of cement to sand when used for plastering?
n: Plaster is commonly mixed 1 part cement to 3 parts sand (Class B). Source: Max Fajardo, Simplified Construction Estimate (Plastering).

q: Which of the following is also called 3D truss?
n: A space frame is a three-dimensional truss: a grid of triangulated members spanning in two directions. Source: Schodek & Bechthold, Structures (Space Frames); Ching, Building Structures Illustrated.

q: Portal framing is ideal for which structure?
n: Portal frames (rigid frames of columns and rafters) give column-free spans, which suits sports halls such as covered basketball courts, warehouses and factories. Source: Ching, Building Structures Illustrated (Rigid Frames); Allen & Iano, Fundamentals of Building Construction.

q: What is the recommended spacing of C-purlins in residential roof framing?
n: Cold-formed C-purlins for residential roofs are commonly spaced about 600 mm on center, depending on the roofing sheet's span rating. Source: Max Fajardo, Simplified Construction Estimate (Roof Framing); roofing manufacturers' span tables.

q: Where can a half truss be placed in a roof framing?
n: Half-truss are usually seen in hipped roofs. They are usually placed on the hips of the roof. Half trusses are set at the hips of a hip roof. They frame the sloping ends between the main trusses and the hip line. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated, Ch. 6 (Hip Roof Framing); Fajardo, Simplified Construction Estimate.

q: The topmost beam in a typical reinforced concrete structural framing for a residential building.
n: Although the tie beam can also be the answer, the roof beam is more correct as the description only describes the position. A tie beam can be placed at any height as long as it functions as a tie beam, connecting the columns together. The roof beam is the topmost beam of an RC frame. It ties the column tops and supports the roof framing. Source: Max Fajardo, Simplified Construction Estimate (RC Framing); Ching, Building Construction Illustrated.

q: What is done to map out the shape and boundaries of a land?
n: A land survey determines and maps the shape, bearings, distances and boundaries of a parcel. A total station is only a tool used in it. Source: Brinker & Wolf, Elementary Surveying; DENR-LMB Manual for Land Surveying.

q: A shallow and broad channel used to convey storm runoff.
n: A swale is a shallow, broad, vegetated channel that conveys and filters stormwater runoff. Source: De Chiara & Koppelman, Time-Saver Standards for Site Planning (Drainage); US EPA, Stormwater BMPs (Grassed Swales).

q: Which is not an ideal height of a panic hardware according to the Fire Code?
n: According to the Fire Code of the Philippines, the height of a panic hardware (bar) shall be 760mm to 1120mm above the floor. Panic hardware bars must be 760–1,120 mm above the floor. 125 mm is far outside that range. Source: RA 9514 (Fire Code) 2019 RIRR (Panic Hardware); NFPA 101, Sec. 7.2.1.7.

q: What should be the maximum difference in height between landing to landing in a staircase?
n: A single flight may rise only about 3.6–3.7 m (12 ft) between landings. Source: RA 9514 (Fire Code) 2019 RIRR, Div. 10.2.5 (Stairs – maximum height between landings); NFPA 101, Table 7.2.2.2.1.1.

q: What is the height of kick plates to protect doors?
n: Kick plates are commonly 250–400 mm high. They protect the lower part of the door from feet and carts, and about 300–400 mm is typical for commercial doors. Source: ANSI/BHMA A156.6 (Architectural Door Trim – Protection Plates).

q: A tight corridor shall be provided with sufficient turning space for wheelchairs every
n: Accessible corridors need turning spaces for wheelchairs at dead ends and at intervals of no more than 12 m. Source: BP 344 IRR, Rule II, Minimum Requirements – Corridors; BP 344 2024 Revised IRR.

q: A cathedral ceiling is best when the roof is
n: A cathedral ceiling follows the underside of a sloping roof. A gable roof gives the classic symmetrical vaulted cathedral ceiling. Source: Ching, A Visual Dictionary of Architecture (Ceiling); Ching, Building Construction Illustrated, Ch. 6.

q: Also known as false ceiling.
n: A dropped (suspended) ceiling, also called a false ceiling, hangs below the structural ceiling and hides services above. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated, Ch. 10 (Suspended Ceilings).

q: A banquette seating is placed
o: At the center of a dining space
n: Banquette seating is a built-in upholstered bench placed along a wall, often with tables in front. Source: Time-Saver Standards for Interior Design (Restaurant Seating); Ching, Interior Design Illustrated.

q: An intermediate level between a floor and a ceiling.
n: A loft is an intermediate upper level or open floor, partly open to the space below, between a floor and the ceiling or roof. Source: Ching, A Visual Dictionary of Architecture; Harris, Dictionary of Architecture and Construction.

q: Which of the following is not a warm color?
n: Red, orange and yellow are warm colors. Green, blue and violet are cool colors. Source: Itten, The Art of Color; Ching, Interior Design Illustrated (Color).

q: Where should air terminals be installed?
n: Air terminals also refer to lightning rods. Air terminals (lightning rods) are installed on the roof and its highest points, such as ridges, parapets and corners, to intercept lightning. Source: NFPA 780 (Lightning Protection Systems); PEC Part 1, Art. 2.80.

q: What is used to hide the curtain rod in the ceiling?
n: A curtain cove is a recess or pocket in the ceiling that hides the curtain rod or track for a clean ceiling line. Source: Ching, Interior Design Illustrated (Window Treatments); interior detailing practice.

q: It is the absorption of all colors.
n: Black absorbs (nearly) all wavelengths of visible light. White reflects them all. Source: Itten, The Art of Color; IES Lighting Handbook (Reflectance).

q: A comparative relationship between two things.
n: Proportion is the comparative relationship of one part to another or to the whole, in size, quantity or degree. Source: Ching, Architecture: Form, Space and Order (Proportion and Scale).

q: Which is not considered as a fixture?
n: Fixtures are attached to the building and usually served by its systems, such as water closets, luminaires and toilet accessories. Wall hangings are loose decor. Source: Ching, Interior Design Illustrated (Furnishings vs. Fixtures).

q: What should be the maximum inclination of escalators?
n: Escalators are normally inclined at a maximum of 30°. A steeper 35° is allowed only for short rises at low speed. The amended BP 344 IRR also caps them at 30°. Source: ASME A17.1 / EN 115-1 (Escalators).

q: Which of the following is a hardware?
n: Door hardware covers the fittings mounted on doors and frames: hinges, locks, closers and stops. The leaf, jamb and frame are the door assembly itself. Source: ANSI/BHMA A156 series (Door Hardware); Ching, Building Construction Illustrated, Ch. 8.

q: Which type of facade treatment fits a government office building?
o: More on concrete instead of glass and steel
More on glass and steel instead of concrete
n: Per the exam key, more glass and steel than solid concrete expresses transparency and openness, which suits a public government office. Source: Goodsell, The Social Meaning of Civic Space; Ching, Architecture: Form, Space and Order (Material and Expression).

q: Where should corner guards be installed?
n: Corner guards protect wall corners and columns from vehicle impact. They are installed in parking areas and other high-impact zones. Source: Time-Saver Standards for Building Types (Parking Structures); NBCP Rule VII (parking provisions).

q: What type of butt hinge is ideal for heavy doors?
n: Ball-bearing butt hinges carry heavy, high-traffic doors with less wear and friction. Plain-bearing hinges are for light doors. Source: ANSI/BHMA A156.1 (Butts and Hinges); Ching, Building Construction Illustrated, Ch. 8.

q: What type of hinge is installed in two mortises between the jamb and door leaf?
n: Invisible (concealed, e.g. SOSS-type) hinges are mortised into both the jamb and the door edge. They are hidden when the door is closed. Source: ANSI/BHMA A156.26 (Continuous and Concealed Hinges); hardware manufacturers' data.

q: What type of hinge is used to install heavy metal gates?
n: Heavy metal gates hang on welded barrel (bullet) hinges, which carry large loads on a pin. Source: Gate hardware references; ANSI/BHMA A156.1.

q: Inset, full overlay and half-overlay are types of which hinge?
n: Concealed cabinet (cup) hinges come in full-overlay, half-overlay and inset versions, according to how the door sits on the carcass. Source: Architectural Woodwork Standards (AWI); hinge manufacturers' catalogs.

q: What is the standard diameter of cup holes?
n: Cup holes are used to install cabinet hinges. Concealed cabinet hinges fit a standard 35 mm cup hole bored into the door. Source: Hinge manufacturers' technical data (35 mm cup standard); Architectural Woodwork Standards.

q: What is the approximate total weight in kg of a W12x36 steel beam 6m long?
n: The designation of a wide flange beam is W(depth) x (unit weight in lbs/ft). Let’?s convert lbs/ft into kg/m. Remember that 1kg = 2.2lbs and 1m = 3.3ft. Therefore, the unit weight is around 54kg/m. Since the beam is 6m, the weight of the wide flange beam is 324kg. W12×36 weighs 36 lb/ft (about 53.6 kg/m). For 6 m: 53.6 × 6 ≈ 321 kg, or roughly 324 kg. Source: AISC Steel Construction Manual, Table 1-1 (W-Shapes).

q: If the project owner decides to put up a 10-room motel structure in the area, how many parking slots would not be enough?
n: See the parking provisions on Table 7.4 of the NBCP for motels, It says there, 1:1 parking provisions shall be considered for motels. Therefore, the minimum shall be 10 units. NBC Table VII.4 requires one parking slot per motel room, so 10 rooms need 10 slots. 9 slots would not be enough. Source: 2004 Revised IRR of PD 1096 (NBCP), Rule VII, Table VII.4 (Parking – Motels).

q: What is the standard moisture content of wood ideal for construction?
n: Construction lumber should be dried to 19% moisture content or less. That is the "dry" grade, which limits shrinkage, warping and decay. Source: USDA Forest Products Laboratory, Wood Handbook, Ch. 4; NSCP 2015, Ch. 6 (Wood).

q: There are 12 boxes of 30cm x 30cm ceramic tiles on site. How much floor area can be covered by these boxes?
n: As a rule of thumb, a box of 30cm x 30cm of ceramic tiles can cover 1 sqm. Therefore, the approximate area that 12 boxes can cover is 12sqm. A box of 30 cm × 30 cm tiles usually holds 11 pieces, about 1 sqm. 12 boxes cover about 12 sqm. Source: Max Fajardo, Simplified Construction Estimate (Tiles); local tile packaging.

q: What is the recommended minimum spacing of downspouts?
n: The recommended spacing of downspouts is between 6m to 15m. Downspouts are commonly spaced about 6 m to 15 m apart, depending on roof area and rainfall intensity. About 6 m is the recommended minimum spacing. Source: Revised National Plumbing Code (Storm Drainage – Rainwater Leaders); SMACNA Architectural Sheet Metal Manual.
